speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources in each of the past three years (a) how much has been spent on the National Recycling Programme; and (b) how many tonnes of recyclables has the programme contributed to the total amount collected from Singapore's domestic recycling sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: NRP was started in 2001 to provide households with a convenient channel to recycle.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: It is complemented by other available recycling channels provided by the private and people sectors, such as charity donation drives, community recycling drives and door-to-door collection of recyclables.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: In recent years, we have been enhancing recycling infrastructure to make it even easier for Singaporeans to recycle.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: These dual chutes have already been introduced in new Housing and Development Board Build-To-Order flats since January 2014.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: We will also use regulatory measures to complement the new recycling infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: For example, we will introduce a new framework to make it easier for Singaporeans to recycle their e-waste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Ultimately, active participation in recycling by all Singaporeans will be key to improving our domestic recycling rates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: The National Environment Agency (NEA) promotes the 3Rs, that is, "reduce, reuse and recycle", via social media posts and educational materials distributed at community and school events.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Information on the proper use of recycling bins, location of collection points and 3R tips are also available on NEA’s website and NEA’s myENV mobile app.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: We will continue to encourage every Singaporean to play their part to reduce, reuse and recycle.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: At the same time, Singaporeans should not misuse the recycling bins.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: A little less-known fact is that we can no longer use the recyclables once they are contaminated, such as by food waste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Let us all be gracious and not waste the efforts of our fellow Singaporeans who want to do their part for the environment.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can I also clarify that the figure that the Senior Minister of State gave of 44,200 tonnes, is that the total amount collected from the Singapore domestic recycling sector or is that the figure that was collected by NRP?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Regarding the question of how much we spent, we do not specifically track the amount spent on outreach programmes and campaigns for NRP because this is actually done in-house by NEA together with other outreach campaigns, such as the Clean and Green Singapore, Keep Singapore Clean and Do the Mozzie Wipeout campaigns.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In addition, NEA does outreach and educational efforts to engage and educate residents on the 3Rs, including NRP through, as I have said, social media posts, as well as on our websites and on our myENV mobile app.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is about 10% of the total amount of recyclables we collect for the domestic sector.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I know that NEA uses surveys to track the proportion of residents who recycle but I do not think it gives a very accurate picture.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, would NEA be conducting more in-depth reviews to evaluate the effectiveness of our recycling programme?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The survey that the Member has referred to is, I think, the PWC Customer Satisfaction Survey.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: That was last done for the period 2015/2016.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We had more than 8,500 respondents who participated in this customer satisfaction survey.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It is done by a consultant using established survey methodologies, so, we think that this is reflective of the level of public participation in recycling.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But we welcome any further suggestions to improve the accuracy of this survey.
